text: Why can silicon not serve as an efficient on-chip laser source?
choices: Its refractive index is too low to confine light
It has an indirect bandgap, so radiative recombination is very inefficient
explanation: Silicon's indirect bandgap forces radiative recombination to involve a phonon, making it a very poor light emitter that cannot lase efficiently, so III-V materials must be integrated for gain. Silicon is actually transparent at 1550 nm, has a high index (3.48), and has a strong thermo-optic effect, so the other options are false.
